title: LTS: add backport PR template, labels, and CODEOWNERS for approval flow
author: Connor O'Brien
body:
Context: As part of the Runtime LTS rollout we need a predictable, auditable approval path for backports into runtime-*-lts branches. This PR introduces (1) a dedicated backport PR template that forces the right metadata (risk tier, issue links, test evidence), (2) a standard set of GitHub labels used by automation + release checklist, and (3) CODEOWNERS adjustments so LTS backports consistently request review from the right owners (runtime kernel/scheduling + release engineering).

Why: Today backports are ad-hoc and we lose time in release week asking the same questions ("what’s the risk tier?", "where’s the perf run?", "which release branch?"). Support feedback also called out that release notes/patch comms need a clear risk tag (SUP-3988).

What changed:
- Add a backport PR template that requires: source PR link, target branch (e.g. runtime-1.20-lts), risk tier (low/med/high), customer impact, test evidence, and rollback plan.
- Add/standardize labels used in the LTS workflow: needs-backport, backport-approved, backport-risk-high, lts-eligible, lts-blocked, release-signoff-required.
- Update CODEOWNERS so changes under runtime kernel/scheduling paths automatically request review from the respective leads + release engineering when the PR is tagged as backport.

Notes:
- This PR does not implement automation (that’s ENG-4823 follow-ups), but it sets the conventions automation will rely on.
- The CODEOWNERS change is scoped to the runtime directories; no global ownership changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Template includes links to Linear + (optional) Jira SUP ticket
- [x] Template includes required perf evidence section for scheduling/kernel changes
- [x] Labels documented with intended meaning
- [x] CODEOWNERS reviewed by Runtime + Release Eng + Security

Rollout:
- Merge to main first; release/* branches will pick up template+labels via tooling in PR #8421 / ENG-4821.

Related:
- ENG-4823 (labeling + automation)
- SUP-3988 (customer request: risk level tagging + clearer notes)
- Runtime LTS docs drafts in progress (Confluence: runtime-lts-backport-policy)
commits: chore(github): add backport PR template with risk tier + evidence sections
chore(github): define LTS/backport labels used by release tooling
chore(ownership): adjust CODEOWNERS for runtime kernel/scheduling + release-eng signoff
conversation:
Noah Patel (review): The template looks good, but can we make the risk tier definitions less subjective? Suggest adding examples of what counts as High (scheduler behavior changes, kernel selection changes, perf-only changes that touch batching) vs Low (logging, metrics, build).

Connor O'Brien (author): Good call. I’ll add an explicit table + examples under the Risk tier section and tie it to the backport policy language.

Sofia Ivanova (review): For scheduling backports we should *require* a perf-canary link, not “if applicable”. We’ve been burned by tiny scheduler diffs causing p99 cliffs.

Connor O'Brien (author): Agree. I’ve updated the template so anything touching scheduling paths requires a perf-canary run link (or an explicit exception with sign-off).

Omar El-Sayed (review): CODEOWNERS change: I’m worried we’re going to pull in too many reviewers on every PR in runtime/. Can we scope ownership only to kernel/scheduling directories and not the whole runtime tree? Also, how do we avoid forcing Release Eng on non-backport runtime PRs?

Connor O'Brien (author): Scoped. Updated CODEOWNERS to target only runtime/kernels/** and runtime/scheduler/**. Release Eng is requested only for backport PRs via template + label + upcoming automation; CODEOWNERS itself no longer adds Release Eng globally.

Sahana Iyer (review): +1. Also please keep label names consistent with what the backport tooling will look for. I suggest prefixing the gating ones with “backport-” so it’s obvious in the UI.

Connor O'Brien (author): I kept needs-backport/backport-approved/backport-risk-high as discussed in #eng-releases; added lts-eligible/lts-blocked for triage. Happy to rename now if you think it’ll reduce confusion.

Sahana Iyer (review): Names look fine; just document them in the repo (docs/process/...).

Marcus Lin (security review): Template asks for “artifact hash” in the evidence section. At PR time we won’t have final artifacts. Recommend wording as “CI attestation link + commit SHA” and leave artifact hashes to the release checklist.

Connor O'Brien (author): Updated. Template now asks for commit SHA + CI run URL; artifact hash collection lives in the release runbook.

Noah Patel (approval): Looks good now. Risk tier examples make this actionable.

Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved. Thanks for scoping CODEOWNERS.

Sofia Ivanova (approval): Approved with the scheduling perf-canary requirement.

Marcus Lin (approval): Approved.

Connor O'Brien (author): Merging (squash) once CI is green.
